label: Engaged liberal rights discourse while exposing colonial-patriarchal collusion in India
description: While drawing on nineteenth-century liberal egalitarian arguments for women's education and self-reliance, Pandita Ramabai demonstrated in The High-Caste Hindu Woman how British colonial courts actively reinforced orthodox patriarchal law rather than liberating Indian women.
dialecticalTension: Exposes the blind spots of metropolitan liberalism when mediated by imperial indirect rule.
historicalContext: Written during Ramabai's travels in Britain and the United States (1883–1888).

label: Provided early South Asian feminist critique of imperial saviorism
description: Postcolonial Indian and transnational feminist scholars, including Chandra Talpade Mohanty, draw on historical figures like Pandita Ramabai to show autonomous South Asian feminist theorizing preceding Western academic feminism.
dialecticalTension: Counters Eurocentric narratives that treat feminism as a late Western export to the Global South.

citations.author: Meera Kosambi
